explanation: Medial medullary syndrome includes: contralateral hemiparesis (pyramidal tract), contralateral loss of proprioception and fine touch (medial lemniscus), and ipsilateral tongue paralysis (hypoglossal nerve).
keyConcept: Medial medullary syndrome - contralateral weakness and proprioception loss

explanation: The medial zone of medulla containing the pyramid is supplied by the anterior spinal artery, which runs in the anterior median fissure. This zone includes the pyramid and medial lemniscus.
keyConcept: Anterior spinal artery supplies medial medulla

explanation: The posterior columns (gracile and cuneate nuclei) are supplied by the posterior spinal arteries and vertebral arteries, NOT by the anterior spinal artery. The anterior spinal supplies the anterior 2/3 of the cord.
keyConcept: Posterior columns not supplied by anterior spinal artery

modelAnswer: VENTRAL SURFACE OF MEDULLA: (1) Two longitudinal elevations: pyramids (anterolateral) containing corticospinal fibers; olives (lateral) containing inferior olivary nuclei. (2) ANTERIOR MEDIAN FISSURE separates the two pyramids. (3) CRANIAL NERVES: XII - emerges between pyramid and olive; IX, X, XI - emerge in groove between olive and inferior cerebellar peduncle.

VENTRAL SURFACE OF PONS: (1) Basilar sulcus - vertical groove for basilar artery. (2) Transverse fibers - connecting cerebrum and cerebellum. (3) CRANIAL NERVES: V (trigeminal) - at junction of pons and middle cerebellar peduncle; VI (abducent) - at pontomedullary junction, medial; VII and VIII - at cerebellopontine angle, lateral.

VENTRAL SURFACE OF MIDBRAIN: (1) Cerebral peduncles (crura cerebri) - two massive bundles separated by interpeduncular fossa; (2) CRANIAL NERVE: III (oculomotor) - emerges from medial aspect of cerebral peduncle; (3) Bands of fibers visible as peduncles descend into pons.

INTERPEDUNCULAR FOSSA: (BOUNDARIES) Anterior - optic chiasma/tract; Posterior - cerebral peduncles; Lateral - optic tract; Inferior - upper border of pons. (CONTENTS) Oculomotor nerve (III), posterior perforated substance, mammillary bodies, tuber cinereum, basilar artery bifurcation.

DORSAL SURFACE OF MEDULLA: (1) Posterior median sulcus and posterior intermediate sulcus divide it into fasciculus gracilis and cuneatus; (2) Gracile tubercle (overlies gracile nucleus) - most medial; (3) Cuneate tubercle (overlies cuneate nucleus); (4) Inferior cerebellar peduncle laterally; (5) Inferior fovea, hypoglossal trigone, vagal trigone, vestibular area.

DORSAL SURFACE OF PONS: (1) Upper part of floor is the tegmentum of pons; (2) Medial eminence (overlying abducent nucleus); (3) Facial colliculus (abducent nucleus + facial nerve fibers); (4) Superior fovea laterally; (5) Locus coeruleus (pigmented cells at upper sulcus limitans); (6) Stria medullaris crossing floor to median sulcus.

DORSAL SURFACE OF MIDBRAIN: (1) Four colliculi (tectal plate) - two superior (visual reflexes) and two inferior (auditory reflexes); (2) Trochlear nerve (IV) emerges below inferior colliculus (only dorsal CN); (3) Cerebral aqueduct connects 3rd and 4th ventricles; (4) Brachium of superior colliculus (to thalamus) and inferior colliculus (to medial geniculate).

ROOF OF 4TH VENTRICLE: (1) Superior medullary velum (superior roof) - connects both superior cerebellar peduncles; (2) Inferior medullary velum (part of inferior roof); (3) Choroid plexus of 4th ventricle (produces CSF); (4) Tectal plate (inferior) - nodulus, uvula, flocculus; (5) Foramina of Luschka (lateral) and Magendie (median) - CSF outflow.

FLOOR OF 4TH VENTRICLE: Divided by median sulcus into right and left halves, each containing: (1) MEDIAL EMINENCE - over abducent nucleus; (2) FACIAL COLLICULUS - formed by facial nerve fibers around abducent nucleus; (3) STRIA MEDULLARIS - entering from cerebellum; (4) SUPERIOR FOVEA; (5) VESTIBULAR AREA - over vestibular nuclei; (6) INFERIOR FOVE A; (7) HYPOGLOSSAL TRIGONE (over hypoglossal nucleus); (8) VAGAL TRIGONE (over dorsal motor nucleus of X); (9) AREA POSTREMA - chemoreceptor trigger zone.

LATERAL BOUNDARIES OF 4TH VENTRICLE: (1) Superior cerebellar peduncle (upper part) - forms lateral walls; (2) Inferior cerebellar peduncle (lower part) - forms lateral walls; (3) Flocculo-nodular lobe of cerebellum; (4) Roots of vestibular and cochlear nerves laterally.

STRUCTURES IN FLOOR OF 4TH VENTRICLE: (From above down, each half): (1) Medial eminence; (2) Facial colliculus; (3) Stria medullaris; (4) Superior fovea; (5) Vestibular area; (6) Inferior fovea; (7) Hypoglossal trigone; (8) Vagal trigone; (9) Area postrema.

LEMNISCI (sensory pathways in brainstem): (1) MEDIAL LEMNISCUS - from dorsal column nuclei (gracile/cuneate) through medulla, pons, midbrain to VPL thalamus; carries conscious proprioception and fine touch. (2) SPINAL LEMNISCUS - from spinothalamic tracts through brainstem to VPL; carries pain and temperature. (3) TRIGEMINAL LEMNISCUS - from trigeminal sensory nuclei to VPM thalamus; carries face sensation. (4) LATERAL LEMNISCUS - auditory pathway from cochlear nuclei to inferior colliculus.

INTERNAL FEATURES OF MEDULLA: (1) PYRAMIDS - contain corticospinal fibers; (2) OLVES - contain inferior olivary nuclei; (3) INTERNAL ARCUATE FIBERS - decussating sensory fibers from dorsal column nuclei; (4) MEDIAL LEMNISCUS - formed after sensory decussation; (5) HYPOGLOSSAL NUCLEUS - in floor near central canal; (6) DORSAL MOTOR NUCLEUS OF X; (7) NUCLEUS SOLITARIUS; (8) NUCLEUS AMBIGUUS; (9) INFERIOR SALIVARY NUCLEUS; (10) INFERIOR CEREBELLAR PEDUNCLES laterally.

PYRAMID AL DECUSSATION: (LOCATION) Caudal medulla; (PROCESS) About 85-90% of corticospinal fibers cross obliquely in the anterior median fissure; (RESULT) Crossed fibers form the lateral corticospinal tract in the lateral white column; uncrossed fibers remain as anterior corticospinal tract; (CLINICAL) Decussation explains contralateral motor control and UMN lesion signs.

SENSORY DECUSSATION: (LOCATION) Caudal medulla; (PROCESS) Second-order neurons from gracile and cuneate nuclei send fibers that become internal arcuate fibers and cross in the medulla; (RESULT) Forms the medial lemniscus which ascends to the contralateral thalamus; (IMPORTANCE) Explains why dorsal column lesions cause ipsilateral sensory loss.

NUCLEI IN MEDULLA: (SOMATIC EFFERENT) Hypoglossal nucleus; (VISCERAL EFFERENT) Dorsal motor nucleus of X, inferior salivary nucleus; (VISCERAL AFFERENT) Nucleus solitarius; (TRIGEMINAL) Spinal nucleus of V; (AUDITORY) Cochlear nuclei; (VESTIBULAR) Vestibular nuclei; (OTHER) Olivary nuclei, cuneate/gracile nuclei, accessory cuneate nucleus.

INFERIOR OLIVARY COMPLEX: (COMPONENTS) Main olivary nucleus (folded gray matter), medial accessory olivary nucleus, dorsal accessory olivary nucleus; (CONNECTIONS) Receives input from red nucleus, spinal cord, and cerebral cortex; (OUTPUT) Olivocerebellar fibers cross and enter cerebellum via inferior cerebellar peduncle; (FUNCTION) Involved in motor learning and coordination.

STRUCTURES IN BASIS PONTIS: (1) Longitudinal fibers - corticopontine, corticospinal, corticobulbar; (2) Transverse fibers - pontocerebellar fibers linking pons with cerebellum; (3) Pontine nuclei - gray matter between fiber bundles; (4) Basilar artery runs in basilar sulcus; (5) CN V attaches at lateral surface.

STRUCTURES IN TEGMENTUM PONTIS: (1) CRANIAL NERVE NUCLEI: Abducent, facial, vestibulocochlear; (2) TRACT: Medial longitudinal fasciculus; (3) LEMNISCI: Medial lemniscus, trigeminal lemniscus; (4) NUCLEI: Superior olivary, cochlear, vestibular, nuclei of reticular formation; (5) PYRAMID does NOT continue here (interrupted by transverse fibers).

PARTS OF MIDBRAIN: (1) TECTUM (quadrigeminal plate) - superior and inferior colliculi; (2) TEGMENTUM - contains crus cerebri, substantia nigra, red nucleus, RAPPORT, medial lemniscus, decussations (superior cerebellar peduncle); (3) CRUS CEREBRI - cerebral peduncle proper, contains descending motor fibers.

CRUS CEREBRI CONTENTS: (MEDIAL 1/5) Frontopontine fibers; (MIDDLE 3/5) Corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers; (LATERAL 1/5) Parietopontine and temporopontine fibers. The corticospinal fibers are somatotopically organized with arm fibers anterior to leg fibers.

TEGMENTAL DECUSSATIONS OF MIDBRAIN: (1) Decussation of superior cerebellar peduncle (dentate nucleus output to thalamus); (2) Decussation of red nucleus (crossing of rubospinal tract fibers); (3) Trochlear nerve decussation (only CN to exit dorsally); (4) Periaqueductal gray matter surrounds cerebral aqueduct.
